documents.title: Renewal net sales after CM EUR 37.9M in FY2026 (+19.9%)
documents.source_ref: Topline Forecast — FC Summary, Renewal Business · Main
documents.excerpt: Main-plan renewals grow from EUR 31.6M (FY2025A) to EUR 37.9M on 274k renewed products (+20.0%). List price holds at about EUR 153; growth is volume from larger cohorts reaching their renewal date.

documents.title: First renewal is the biggest leak: 73.9% vs 81.3% retention
documents.source_ref: Renew — Retention sheet, 12-month term, youngest vs older cohorts
documents.excerpt: Customers renewing for the first time retain at 73.9% on 12-month terms and 67.4% on 24-month terms, against 81.3% and 73.5% for older cohorts. Each point of retention across cohorts is worth about EUR 0.7M of FY2027 renewal net sales.

documents.title: Credit memos fall from EUR 1.20M to EUR 1.07M
documents.source_ref: Net Sales after CM — Renewal Business · Main
documents.excerpt: Credit memo sales on renewals improve by EUR 0.13M year on year and drop to EUR 0.34M in FY2027 in the plan. The forecast assumes refunds on auto-renewals fall sharply; that assumption carries the most risk in the renewal bridge.

documents.title: Addon renewals discounted 6.3% vs 2.7% on main plans
documents.source_ref: FC Summary — Discount Rate, Renewal Business · Addon vs Main
documents.excerpt: Addon renewals (437k products, list price EUR 16.4) carry a 6.3% discount rate, more than twice the main-plan rate. Aligning addon discounts to 4% adds about EUR 0.18M of FY2026 net sales.

documents.title: Retention multiplier +2pp from 2027 is worth about EUR 1.4M
documents.excerpt: The workbook scenario lifts retention by 0.2pp in 2026 and 2pp from 2027. On 329k FY2027 renewals at a EUR 126 net price, +2pp adds about EUR 1.4M of renewal net sales after CM — the ML forecast tests whether the cohort history supports it.
